params.q: How many weeks of paid maternity leave are women entitled to in India?

search_parameters.q: How many weeks of paid maternity leave are women entitled to in India?

text_blocks.snippet: In India, under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (amended in 2017), women are entitled to paid maternity leave based on specific conditions:

list.snippet: 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for up to their first two surviving children (can be claimed up to 8 weeks before expected delivery). You can review the official framework details on the National Commission for Women Booklet.
12 weeks of paid maternity leave for women who already have two or more surviving children.
12 weeks of paid maternity leave for adoptive mothers (for a child under the age of three months) and commissioning mothers (surrogacy), calculated from the date the child is handed over.
6 weeks of paid leave in the case of a miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy.

2 weeks of extra paid leave in the case of a tubectomy operation, and additional leave up to 30 days for specific medical illnesses arising out of pregnancy, delivery, premature birth, or miscarriage.

text_blocks.snippet: To qualify, a woman must have worked in an establishment (with 10 or more employees) for at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding the date of her expected delivery.
Would you like to know more about the eligibility criteria, employer obligations, or provisions for work-from-home and nursing breaks?

In India, under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 \(amended in 2017\), women are entitled to paid maternity leave based on specific conditions: [0]

- 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for up to their first two surviving children \(can be claimed up to 8 weeks before expected delivery\). You can review the official framework details on the [National Commission for Women Booklet](https://cdn.ncw.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Maternity-bookletA5-14.8-by-21-cm-13-feb_compressed.pdf). [0] [1]
- 12 weeks of paid maternity leave for women who already have two or more surviving children. [1]
- 12 weeks of paid maternity leave for adoptive mothers \(for a child under the age of three months\) and commissioning mothers \(surrogacy\), calculated from the date the child is handed over. [1]
- 6 weeks of paid leave in the case of a miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy. [2]
- 2 weeks of extra paid leave in the case of a tubectomy operation, and additional leave up to 30 days for specific medical illnesses arising out of pregnancy, delivery, premature birth, or miscarriage.

To qualify, a woman must have worked in an establishment \(with 10 or more employees\) for at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding the date of her expected delivery. [0] [2]
